name: The Quantum Pi Benchmark
description: This paper takes the first step towards hardware evidence for The Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB) under its provenance (P) and blindness (B) axes and non-total capability grid (R). Using IBM Heron r2 Quantum Processing Units (QPUs), this paper reports findings to support P0/B0/R2 compiled-address amplification and P1/B0/R3 only for the loaded-content equality-predicate family, spanning 220 logical results and 324 job records. In the compiled-address family, single-iteration efficiency is approximately 66% through 110 routed CZ gates and falls to roughly 15% at the traceable larger instances. The two recoverable N = 512, k = 1 executions used 270 CZ gates and returned 84 marked outcomes in 32,768 shots, or 0.256% (95% Wilson interval 0.207%–0.317%), 1.31 times the uniform expectation. Matched true, scrambled, and zero controls show that this signal amplifies a compiled mark rather than evaluating Pi content. A content-addressed Quantum Read Only Memory (QROM) bridge and a coherent block-equality negative result are retained as P1/B0 diagnostics. Loaded-content equality separates supplied Pi blocks from corrupted controls: the monolithic discrimination gap decreases from 0.780 at six bits to 0.132 at 24 bits. Across three matched transpiler placements, tiled equality gives gaps of 0.761 ± 0.004, 0.404 ± 0.153, 0.344 ± 0.037, and 0.128 ± 0.034 at 6, 12, 18, and 24 bits, respectively, where uncertainties are descriptive sample standard deviations.
